seoTitle: Why Can't I Go Live on Instagram? 6 Fixes That Work
metaDescription: Instagram Live greyed out or missing? Check the 1,000-follower and public-account requirement first, then Account Status, app version, permissions and connection.
intro: Tapping the plus button and finding no Live option, or watching it fail the moment you start, is one of the more frustrating Instagram problems, because the app rarely explains why. Instagram also quietly raised the bar for who can go Live at all, so an account that had the feature before can lose it without doing anything wrong. This guide checks that new requirement first, then works through account restrictions, an outdated app, missing camera or microphone permissions, a weak connection, and a corrupted local cache, in the order that finds the real answer fastest.

steps.heading: Start from your profile and open Settings
steps.body: Everything here starts on your own profile tab, the one with your posts, follower count, and the Edit profile and Share profile buttons. A creator or business account also shows a Professional dashboard panel here, and account warnings sometimes surface in it first. Note whether Live appears at all when you tap the plus button: an option that's missing entirely points to an eligibility or account problem, covered next, while one that appears but fails when tapped points to permissions or connectivity further down this guide. Open the menu at the top right to reach Settings, which is where every check below starts.

image.caption: The profile tab where the fix starts, with the Professional dashboard panel and the menu button that leads into Settings.

steps.heading: Check the two hard eligibility requirements
steps.body: Instagram tightened who can use Live at all. Meta confirmed to TechCrunch that, since August 2025, an account needs to be public and have at least 1,000 followers to start a Live video; accounts under that bar see the option greyed out or missing, with an in-app notice reading "Only public accounts with 1,000 followers or more will be able to create live videos." There's no workaround beyond switching to public and building the follower count. Separately, Instagram turns Live off by default for anyone under 16 on a Teen Account; a parent or guardian has to grant permission through Teen Account supervision before it becomes available, while 16- and 17-year-olds get Live without that step but still have content-safety filters applied. If either of these applies to you, nothing later in this guide brings Live back.

steps.heading: Check Account Status for a content violation
steps.body: If both eligibility checks above are clear, open Settings, tap Account, then tap Account Status. It sits there now, not under a general "More info and support" menu; older instructions that send you looking there are describing an earlier layout. Account Status shows whether Instagram has removed any of your content, which features are restricted, and whether your account currently qualifies for recommendations and features like Live. A community-guideline strike will often disable Live with no separate notification, so people spend hours on other fixes when the answer was already on this page. If Account Status shows a violation, use the Request a Review link there; a successful appeal can take a little time to take effect before Live comes back.

image.caption: Account Status, now reached through Settings > Account instead of a general support menu.

steps.heading: Update the app and confirm camera and microphone access
steps.body: If Account Status is clean, update Instagram from the App Store or Play Store; Instagram changes Live regularly, and an old build can lose the feature or crash when a stream starts. Restart the app fully afterward by swiping it out of the recent apps list instead of just returning to the home screen. Then confirm Live's two permissions are genuinely granted: on Android, go to Settings, then Apps, then Instagram, then Permissions, and check that Camera and Microphone are allowed; on iPhone, open Settings and scroll to Instagram in the app list for the same two toggles. If they're already on, turn them off and back on. A stale permission grant occasionally needs resetting before the app notices it.

steps.heading: Rule out the connection
steps.body: Live streaming needs sustained upload bandwidth, not just a connection that technically works. A Wi-Fi network that loads Reels fine can still be too slow upstream to hold a broadcast, which is why Live sometimes starts and then drops after a few seconds. Switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data, or the reverse, and try again; that single swap resolves a good share of cases. Turning airplane mode on for a few seconds and back off also forces a fresh network handshake, which helps when the phone is holding onto a weak signal.

steps.heading: Clear the cache or reinstall as a last resort
steps.body: If Live still won't start, the app's local data is the last thing left to reset. On Android, go to Settings, then Apps, then Instagram, then Storage, and tap Clear cache; this removes temporary files without touching your login or content. On iPhone there's no cache button, so the equivalent is deleting Instagram and installing it again, which wipes the same local state. Neither action deletes your account, posts, followers or messages, since all of that lives on Instagram's servers, not your phone. Log back in, open your profile, and try Live once more.

troubleshooting.problem: Live vanished from the plus-button menu with no explanation
troubleshooting.cause: Instagram now requires a public account with 1,000 or more followers to use Live; accounts below that threshold lose the option outright, even if they used it before.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch the account to public and build past 1,000 followers. There's no bypass. If real-time contact matters more than the follower count, a Reel or a video call is the closer substitute for now.

troubleshooting.problem: Live is greyed out on a teenager's account
troubleshooting.cause: Instagram turns Live off by default for anyone under 16 on a Teen Account.
troubleshooting.fix: Have a parent or guardian set up Teen Account supervision and approve the Live permission from their side.

troubleshooting.problem: Account Status shows a violation and Live still hasn't returned after appealing
troubleshooting.cause: Eligibility takes a little time to update once a review clears.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait and re-check Account Status; there's no faster path inside the app.

faq.question: Why did Live disappear even though I used it before?
faq.answer: Instagram now requires a public account with at least 1,000 followers to go Live, a change Meta confirmed in August 2025. Accounts that fall under that bar lose the option even if they had it earlier, with an on-screen notice explaining the new requirement.

faq.question: How do I check if Instagram restricted my account?
faq.answer: Open your profile, tap the menu, go into Settings, then Account, then Account Status. It lists any violations, which content caused them, and whether your account currently qualifies for features like Live.

faq.question: Do I need a minimum number of followers to go live on Instagram?
faq.answer: Yes. As of the August 2025 policy change, you need a public account and at least 1,000 followers. This is a hard requirement, not a soft recommendation.

faq.question: Can teenagers go live on Instagram?
faq.answer: 16- and 17-year-olds can, with content-safety filters applied. Anyone under 16 has Live turned off by default and needs a parent or guardian to approve it through Teen Account supervision first.

faq.question: Does reinstalling Instagram delete my posts or followers?
faq.answer: No. Reinstalling clears only the app's local cache and settings on your phone. Your account, posts, followers, saved items and messages are stored on Instagram's servers and return when you log in again.

faq.question: Instagram Live starts and then cuts out after a few seconds, what's wrong?
faq.answer: That pattern almost always points at upload bandwidth, not the app. Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, move closer to your router, and try again; a connection can load your feed fine and still be too slow to sustain a broadcast.

verifiedNote: Click paths, screenshots and the original list of causes come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. The Account Status navigation path and the two Live-eligibility gates, the 1,000-follower public-account minimum and the under-16 guardian requirement, were checked against Instagram's own Account Status page, Meta's April 2025 Teen Accounts announcement and Meta's confirmation to TechCrunch of the August 2025 change, in September 2026. Both eligibility gates were missing from the previous draft; they're now the first thing this guide checks, and the Account Status path itself moved from a general support menu to Settings > Account > Account Status.
